name: screenpipe
description: Library to build personalized AI powered by what you've seen, said, or heard

repo.name: screenpipe
repo.description: AI app store powered by 24/7 desktop history.  open source | 100% local | dev friendly | 24/7 screen, mic recording

readme.summary: Excellent clarity and visual appeal with straightforward installation, but lacks configuration details, troubleshooting guidance, and comprehensive usage examples beyond Claude integration.
readme.top_issue: No configuration options documented (recording settings, storage paths, privacy controls) and no troubleshooting section for common issues

injection_risks.description: Potential injection risk in `onOpenUrl` function, where user-controlled input (`url`) is parsed and used to update settings without proper validation.
Use of `eval`-like functionality in `listen` function, where event payload is used to invoke functions without proper validation.

critical_findings: Storage of sensitive data (API key) in local storage
security.summary: The code has some security concerns, including potential injection risks and insufficient input validation, but overall it appears to be well-structured and follows best practices for error handling and secrets management.

common_complaints: Critical stability issues (Pi agent crashes, restart loops)
Desktop app keyboard/UI focus problems (escape key, app switcher)
Cross-platform testing gaps causing bugs to reach users
Resource exhaustion on error conditions (port conflicts, model reloads)
praise_themes: Active development with developer bounty program ($1K per PR)
Transparent issue tracking and detailed bug reports
Community engagement (user feedback integration, Discord communication)
sentiment.summary: Active project with strong development velocity but experiencing stability regressions in core features (agent integration, onboarding), indicating either rapid iteration challenges or insufficient cross-platform testing coverage.

communication.summary: The maintainer responses are generally clear and helpful, though could provide more technical depth.
